CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
[redacted location] Hospital NHS Trust

QF-PCR ANEUPLOIDY SCREENING REPORT

Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sample Type: Uncultured placental material
Clinical Details: Fetal loss investigation
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured placental material to detect aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 15, 16, 18, 21, 22, X and Y using fluorescently labeled microsatellite markers. DNA was extracted and amplified using multiplex PCR with chromosome-specific STR markers. Fragment analysis was performed on an Applied Biosystems genetic analyzer.

MARKERS ANALYZED
Chromosome 21: D21S11, D21S1409, D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1446
Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S305, D13S628, D13S634
Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
Chromosome X: AMELX, DXS6803, DXS6809, HPRT
Chromosome Y: AMELY, SRY
Chromosomes 15, 16, 22: Multiple STR markers

RESULTS

**ABNORMAL RESULT - TRISOMY 21 DETECTED**

Chromosome 21: TRISOMY
- D21S11: Three alleles detected (ratio 1:1:1)
- D21S1409: Three alleles detected (ratio 1:1:1)
- D21S1435: Three alleles detected (ratio 1:1:1)
- D21S1411: Three alleles detected (ratio 1:1:1)
- D21S1446: Uninformative (homozygous)

Chromosome 13: NORMAL DISOMIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal biallelic ratios

Chromosome 15: NORMAL DISOMIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal biallelic ratios

Chromosome 16: NORMAL DISOMIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal biallelic ratios

Chromosome 18: NORMAL DISOMIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal biallelic ratios

Chromosome 22: NORMAL DISOMIC PATTERN
All informative markers show normal biallelic ratios

Sex Chromosomes: FEMALE (XX)
AMELX present, AMELY absent
X chromosome markers show normal female pattern

Triploidy Assessment: NO EVIDENCE OF TRIPLOIDY
Normal diallelic patterns observed for all informative autosomal markers

MOLECULAR KARYOTYPE
rsa(X,13,15,16,18)×2,(21)×3,(22)×2

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR analysis has detected trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in the fetal tissue sample. Four informative markers on chromosome 21 (D21S11, D21S1409, D21S1435, D21S1411) each show three distinct alleles in a 1:1:1 ratio, confirming the presence of three copies of chromosome 21.

The remaining chromosomes tested (13, 15, 16, 18, 22, X) show normal copy number. The fetus was female with a normal XX sex chromosome complement. No evidence of triploidy was detected.

Trisomy 21 is the most likely etiology for the fetal loss in this case. Down syndrome occurs in approximately 1 in 700 live births but is more common in early pregnancy losses.

LIMITATIONS
- This test only detects numerical abnormalities of the specified chromosomes
- Structural rearrangements, mosaicism <20%, and abnormalities of other chromosomes are not detected
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be excluded without comparative analysis

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Parental blood samples are requested for chromosome analysis to exclude a balanced chromosome rearrangement that may increase recurrence risk
2. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss results and recurrence risks
3. The empiric recurrence risk for trisomy 21 is approximately 1% above the maternal age-related risk

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
